definition: A plant's bundled price for a finished record: lacquers, plating, labels, sleeves and a printed jacket.
The coated disc a mastering engineer cuts the grooves into; the first physical copy of a record, and a line item on plant price cards.
Making metal parts from the lacquer to produce stampers; 3-step adds a metal mother so more stampers can be made for bigger runs.
The metal negative that presses the grooves into the plastic.
The lump of PVC placed in the press before it is squeezed into a record.
A small number of early copies the artist plays and approves before the full run.
An older jacket construction with printed paper glued over board.
The time from an approved order to delivery; one US plant listed 6-8 weeks as standard in 2026.
A paid faster turnaround, priced per record.
The same album in a different color, cover or retailer-exclusive edition.
Luminate's measure combining album sales with streams and track downloads.
Physical and digital album purchases only, without streams.
Polyvinyl chloride, the plastic most records are pressed from.
PVC made with renewable feedstock, such as used cooking oil, in place of petroleum.
A certification for sustainable and circular supply chains, used for BioVinyl.
Forcing molten material into a mold, used by Green Vinyl Records in place of steam presses.
A record pressed from a non-PVC plastic, such as Evolution Music's sugar-and-starch recipe.
